messages:
Ravi (Finance): Received invoice from BuenosData (BD-AR-55). They labeled it 'IVA exento' and added a note: 'Please gross-up 15% for local withholding'. Invoice total USD 5,600. Can AP pay this as-is?
Priya (Accounts Payable): Do we have their CUIT or AFIP comprobante? For Argentinian suppliers we usually need factura electrónica (CAE) or a registrada invoice. Also W-8/W-9 not relevant.
Lucia (Vendor Ops): Vendor says services performed in Argentina (Buenos Aires). They attached only a PDF invoice with a handwritten note about gross-up, no tax certificates.
Diego (Legal): We need formal docs before altering payment. Ask for: (1) CUIT and AFIP registration or factura electrónica with CAE code; (2) comprobante de retención or proof of payment to AFIP if they claim a withholding has already been applied; (3) if they want us to gross-up, a contractual amendment or explicit clause plus a worked gross-up calculation.
TaxBot: Auto-check: CUIT format looks like 11 digits (e.g., 30-70876543-2). No proof attached. Argentina standard IVA is 21% for most services; withholdings/percepciones vary by province and payer status. A vendor can't unilaterally ask for gross-up without documentation. Recommend hold payment.
Ravi (Finance): Action items: Lucia request the AFIP factura electrónica or CAE, a retencion/comprobante if they already paid, and a clear gross-up calculation with legal basis. Priya will block payment until docs received.
Priya (Accounts Payable): Blocking payment in AP now and flagging item as 'awaiting AFIP docs'. If they push the gross-up, we'll need Legal + Finance sign-off.
Lucia (Vendor Ops): Message sent to vendor (pasted):
```
Hola BuenosData,

Thanks for the invoice. To process payment we require the following within 72 hours:
1) CUIT (AFIP tax ID) and a copy of your AFIP registration;
2) factura electrnica with CAE code or an AFIP-registered invoice;
3) If you claim a withholding/retencin has been applied, please provide the comprobante de retencin or proof of remittance to AFIP tied to this invoice;
4) If you expect Redwood to gross-up the amount, provide the legal basis and a worked example calculation and a proposed contract amendment authorizing the gross-up.

Please respond ASAP so we can proceed.
```
Diego (Legal): If they provide AFIP remittance that specifically ties to this invoice period we'll consider accepting post-payment substantiation, but we won't increase payment amounts without a signed amendment. Also ask vendor to state the place of performance on the invoice (city/country) to help determine whether Argentine-source rules apply.
TaxBot: Note: if services were performed outside Argentina, withholding may not apply. Request vendor state location of service delivery explicitly.
Ravi (Finance): Thanks. I'll prep a quick gross-up worksheet in case Legal requests modeling. Lucia, ping here when vendor replies. :memo:
